title: Thresholded cardiac reversals show asymmetric, calibration-sensitive age transfer between two public ECG collections
abstract: A fixed 20-ms hard RR reversal feature gave asymmetric, calibration-sensitive cross-collection age classification gains. Fantasia-to-NSR2 log loss fell from 0.839743 to 0.633772 (gain 0.205971; joint-refit 95% interval [0.017106,0.516023]), but AUC changed only 0.876744 to 0.879070 and reverse-transfer loss increased by 0.047961. Oracle target-intercept recalibration reduced forward gain to 0.009504; timestamp rounding and comparator choice materially changed the result. This does not establish a portable aging or clinical biomarker; participant overlap is unverified.
